note.question: How should a seller choose loot-box price and product-allocation probabilities, when will consumers repeatedly purchase, and when can probabilistic selling outperform deterministic pricing in profit and welfare?
note.overview: The paper is an incentive-compatible screening and mechanism-design model. A monopolist commits to price and allocation probabilities, heterogeneous consumers optimally self-select into single or repeated purchase paths, and the firm solves a constrained mechanism problem using their individual-rationality and incentive constraints.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The firm first commits to a single loot-box price p and announced probability phi of product 1 (and 1-phi of product 2). Consumers observe the mechanism and decide whether to buy. After each purchase the product outcome is revealed; loyal consumers dynamically decide whether to stop or buy again, taking future repurchases into account, while switchers buy at most once in the focal profitable regime. The firm chooses p and phi anticipating these self-selection and continuation decisions. seller commitment to a probabilistic allocation and common price consumer-type self-selection into no purchase, one purchase, or repeated purchase
